provenance.basis: New variants developed from Maths4U own skill briefs and independently authored checks; no examination question text
provenance.verification: Arithmetic witnesses, numerical/domain tests, canonical grading and browser verification; independent teacher review pending

grading_policy: One point for the final short answer or selected option. Does not assess proof or written reasoning. Numeric tolerance is absolute 0.000001; decimals to at least six places or a number/fraction. No general expression evaluation.

questions.title: Factorisation and valid roots: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(x^2-2x-15=0\), enter the positive root.
questions.hint_html: Factor the quadratic into two linear factors.

questions.title: Factorisation and valid roots: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(3x^2-7x-6=0\), enter the negative root.
questions.hint_html: A factorisation must reproduce both the middle and constant terms.

questions.title: Factorisation and valid roots: review variant 3
questions.focus: do not divide away a root
questions.prompt_html: How many distinct real roots does \(x(x+7)=0\) have?
questions.hint_html: Use both factors; do not divide by x.
questions.solution_html: The roots are \(0\) and \(-7\), so there are two.

questions.title: Factorisation and valid roots: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\frac{x^2-16}{x-4}=0\). Enter the admissible root.
questions.hint_html: The original denominator excludes one numerator root.
questions.solution_html: The numerator vanishes at \(\pm4\), but \(x=4\) is excluded. Only \(-4\) is allowed.

questions.title: Completing the square and range: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Write \(x^2-8x+3=(x-p)^2+q\), where \(p>0\). Find \(p\).
questions.hint_html: Halve the x coefficient, retaining the bracket sign.

questions.title: Completing the square and range: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the minimum of \(3x^2+12x+19\).
questions.hint_html: Take out the coefficient 3 before completing the square.

questions.title: Completing the square and range: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the maximum of \(-2x^2+8x\).
questions.hint_html: A negative multiple of a real square is non-positive.

questions.title: Completing the square and range: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: How many distinct real roots does \(-2(x+3)^2+7=7\) have?
questions.hint_html: Isolate the square.
questions.solution_html: \((x+3)^2=0\), so there is one distinct root, \(x=-3\).

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the discriminant of \(3x^2-9x+6\).
questions.hint_html: Calculate b squared minus 4ac.

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: For which \(k\) does \(x^2-6x+k=0\) have a repeated root?
questions.hint_html: A repeated root has zero discriminant.

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: How many distinct real roots does \(x^4-9x^2=0\) have?
questions.hint_html: Factor in x squared, remembering that zero is one distinct root.

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: For \(x-5\sqrt{x}+6=0\), enter the larger real solution.
questions.hint_html: Put u = square root of x with u non-negative.

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: review variant 5
questions.prompt_html: Use the quadratic formula to find the larger root of \(2x^2-5x+1=0\). Enter a decimal to at least six places.
questions.hint_html: The discriminant is 17 and the denominator is 4.
questions.solution_html: \(x=(5\pm\sqrt{17})/4\), so the larger root is approximately \(2.2807764064\).

questions.title: Quadratic inequalities and integer constraints: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: For \((x-1)(x-6)<0\), enter the lower endpoint of the solution interval.
questions.hint_html: The quadratic is negative between its roots.
questions.solution_html: The solution is \(1<x<6\). The lower endpoint is \(1\), which is excluded.

questions.title: Quadratic inequalities and integer constraints: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(x^2-16\ge0\), enter the smallest non-negative solution.
questions.hint_html: Include the boundary roots.
questions.solution_html: The solution is \(x\le-4\) or \(x\ge4\). The requested value is \(4\).

questions.title: Quadratic inequalities and integer constraints: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: How many integers satisfy \(x^2-2x-15<0\)?
questions.hint_html: Factor and count the integers strictly between the roots.

questions.title: Quadratic inequalities and integer constraints: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: How many real numbers satisfy \(-(x+4)^2\ge0\)?
questions.hint_html: The expression is at most zero, so equality is required.
questions.solution_html: Only \(x=-4\) makes the square zero; there is one solution.

questions.title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x+6\) and \(y=x^2\), enter the larger intersection x-coordinate.
questions.hint_html: Equate the y expressions.

questions.title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x+4\), \(x^2+y^2=16\), one intersection has \(x=0\). Find the other x-coordinate.
questions.hint_html: Substitute the line into the circle.

questions.title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: How many intersections do \(y=2x-1\) and \(y=x^2+1\) have?
questions.hint_html: Check the discriminant after substitution.
questions.solution_html: \(x^2-2x+2=0\) has discriminant \(-4\), so there are no real intersections.

questions.title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: The line \(y=6x+k\) is tangent to \(y=x^2\). Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Tangency gives a repeated quadratic root.

questions.title: Inverse functions, domain and range: review variant 1
questions.hint_html: Solve f(x)=11.

questions.title: Inverse functions, domain and range: review variant 2
questions.hint_html: Reverse the operations by solving for the original input.

questions.title: Inverse functions, domain and range: review variant 3
questions.hint_html: Cross-multiply and check the excluded denominator.

questions.title: Inverse functions, domain and range: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: How many real inputs of \(h(x)=x^2\) give output 25?
questions.hint_html: Both signs can give the same square.
questions.solution_html: \(x=\pm5\), two inputs. Thus h is not one-to-one on all real numbers.

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: review variant 1
questions.hint_html: Use the inner function first.

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: review variant 2
questions.hint_html: Composition order matters.

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{x}\), \(g(x)=x-7\), enter the lower endpoint of the real domain of \(f(g(x))\).
questions.hint_html: The square-root argument must be non-negative.

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Let \(f(x)=2x\) on \([0,a]\), \(a>0\), and let g have domain \([0,10]\). Find the greatest a for which \(g\circ f\) is defined for every input of f.
questions.hint_html: The range of f must fit inside the domain of g.
questions.solution_html: The range of f is \([0,2a]\). We need \(2a\le10\), so the greatest a is \(5\).

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: review variant 5
questions.prompt_html: For \(f(x)=3/x\), \(x\ge2\), enter the upper endpoint of its range.
questions.hint_html: The reciprocal decreases as positive x increases.
questions.solution_html: The range is \((0,3/2]\); its upper endpoint \(3/2\) is attained at x=2.

questions.title: Restricting a quadratic to obtain an inverse: review variant 1
questions.hint_html: Use the branch compatible with x at least 4.

questions.title: Restricting a quadratic to obtain an inverse: review variant 2
questions.hint_html: The left branch uses a negative square root.

questions.title: Restricting a quadratic to obtain an inverse: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: For \(h(x)=(x+1)^2-3\), \(x\ge-1\), enter the lower endpoint of the range.
questions.hint_html: Find when the square is zero.

questions.title: Restricting a quadratic to obtain an inverse: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: For \(f(x)=x^2\) restricted to \(x\le0\), find \(f^{-1}(49)\).
questions.hint_html: The restriction selects one of the two square roots.
questions.solution_html: The allowed original input is \(-7\), not \(7\).

questions.title: A function and its inverse on a graph: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: The graph of f contains \((6,-5)\). Find the corresponding inverse-graph x-coordinate.
questions.hint_html: Swap the coordinates.

questions.title: A function and its inverse on a graph: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Reflect \((-4,9)\) in the line \(y=x\). Enter the image y-coordinate.
questions.hint_html: Reflection in the inverse mirror line swaps x and y.

questions.title: A function and its inverse on a graph: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: For \(f(x)=4x-9\), find the x-coordinate of its fixed point.
questions.hint_html: At a fixed point f(x)=x.

questions.title: A function and its inverse on a graph: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A one-to-one function has range \([8,\infty)\). Enter the smallest allowed input of its inverse.
questions.hint_html: The inverse domain equals the original range.
questions.solution_html: The inverse domain is \([8,\infty)\), whose minimum is \(8\).

questions.title: Transformations, stretches and coordinate rules: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Point \((3,5)\) lies on \(y=f(x)\). For \(y=f(x+4)\), find the image x-coordinate.
questions.hint_html: An inside +4 shifts the graph left 4.

questions.title: Transformations, stretches and coordinate rules: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Point \((2,-2)\) lies on \(y=f(x)\). For \(y=-3f(x)+1\), find the image y-coordinate.
questions.hint_html: Apply the outside operations to the output.

questions.title: Transformations, stretches and coordinate rules: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A point on \(y=f(x)\) has x-coordinate 12. Find its image x-coordinate on \(y=f(4x)\).
questions.hint_html: Horizontal coordinates divide by the inside multiplier.

questions.title: Transformations, stretches and coordinate rules: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Point \((2,-3)\) lies on \(y=f(x)\). For \(y=-f(x-2)+5\), find the image y-coordinate.
questions.hint_html: The outside operations determine the new y-coordinate.

questions.title: Distance, midpoint and geometric reasoning: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the distance between \((1,-2)\) and \((6,10)\).
questions.hint_html: Use coordinate differences as the legs of a right triangle.

questions.title: Distance, midpoint and geometric reasoning: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the midpoint y-coordinate for \((-4,-7)\), \((8,3)\).
questions.hint_html: Average the two y-coordinates.

questions.title: Distance, midpoint and geometric reasoning: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: \((4,3)\) is the midpoint of \((-1,5)\) and B. Find the x-coordinate of B.
questions.hint_html: Twice the midpoint is the sum of the endpoints.

questions.title: Distance, midpoint and geometric reasoning: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A point \((x,7)\) is equidistant from \((1,0)\) and \((9,0)\). Find x.
questions.hint_html: Use the perpendicular bisector of the horizontal segment.

questions.title: Parallel, perpendicular and exceptional lines: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the gradient of a line perpendicular to \(y=-3x+2\).
questions.hint_html: Perpendicular non-vertical gradients have product -1.

questions.title: Parallel, perpendicular and exceptional lines: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the gradient of a line parallel to \(3x+4y=12\).
questions.hint_html: Rearrange the equation into slope-intercept form.
questions.solution_html: \(y=-3x/4+3\), so a parallel line has gradient \(-3/4\).

questions.title: Parallel, perpendicular and exceptional lines: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A line is perpendicular to \(x=-2\) and passes through \((5,6)\). Find its y-intercept.
questions.hint_html: A line perpendicular to a vertical line is horizontal.
questions.solution_html: The required line is \(y=6\), with y-intercept \(6\).

questions.title: Parallel, perpendicular and exceptional lines: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Find the gradient perpendicular to the line through \((1,2)\) and \((7,5)\).
questions.hint_html: Find the original gradient, then its negative reciprocal.
questions.solution_html: The original gradient is \(3/6=1/2\); the perpendicular gradient is \(-2\).

questions.title: Straight-line equations, intercepts and intersections: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: A line has gradient -2 and passes through \((3,2)\). Find its y-intercept.
questions.hint_html: Substitute the point into y=-2x+c.

questions.title: Straight-line equations, intercepts and intersections: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the gradient through \((-2,-3)\) and \((3,7)\).
questions.hint_html: Divide the y difference by the x difference.

questions.title: Straight-line equations, intercepts and intersections: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the intersection x-coordinate of \(y=2x+1\) and \(y=5x-8\).
questions.hint_html: Equate the expressions for y.

questions.title: Straight-line equations, intercepts and intersections: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A vertical line passes through \((7,-3)\). It has equation \(x=k\). Find k.
questions.hint_html: Every point on a vertical line has the same x-coordinate.

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the radius of \((x+3)^2+(y-1)^2=36\).
questions.hint_html: The right side is the radius squared.

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the centre x-coordinate of \(x^2+y^2+4x-10y+4=0\).
questions.hint_html: Complete the x square.

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A diameter has endpoints \((0,0)\), \((10,24)\). Find the radius.
questions.hint_html: The radius is half the diameter length.

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Find the tangent gradient to \(x^2+y^2=25\) at \((4,3)\).
questions.hint_html: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
questions.solution_html: The radius gradient is \(3/4\), so the tangent gradient is \(-4/3\).

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: review variant 5
questions.prompt_html: AB is a circle diameter. C is another point on the circle. If angle ABC is \(28^\circ\), find angle BAC in degrees.
questions.hint_html: The angle at C is a right angle.

questions.title: Line–circle intersections, chords and tangency: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: How many intersections do \(y=6\), \(x^2+y^2=36\) have?
questions.hint_html: Substitute the line into the circle.
questions.solution_html: \(x^2=0\), so there is just one intersection, \((0,6)\).

questions.title: Line–circle intersections, chords and tangency: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the chord length cut by \(y=12\) on \(x^2+y^2=169\).
questions.hint_html: Find both intersection x-coordinates.

questions.title: Line–circle intersections, chords and tangency: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: How many real intersections do \(x=7\), \(x^2+y^2=64\) have?
questions.hint_html: Compare the line distance from the centre with the radius.

questions.title: Line–circle intersections, chords and tangency: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: The line \(y=k\), k positive, is tangent to \(x^2+y^2=81\). Find k.
questions.hint_html: A tangent horizontal line is one radius from the centre.

questions.title: Radians, degrees and complete rotations: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Write \(105^\circ=k\pi\) radians. Find k.
questions.hint_html: Multiply by pi/180.

questions.title: Radians, degrees and complete rotations: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Convert \(7\pi/4\) radians to degrees.
questions.hint_html: Multiply by 180/pi.

questions.title: Radians, degrees and complete rotations: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: An arc has length 18 cm on a radius-8 cm circle. Find its angle in radians.
questions.hint_html: Divide arc length by radius.

questions.title: Radians, degrees and complete rotations: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A sector has angle 2 radians and radius 5 cm. Find its arc length in cm.
questions.hint_html: The arc-length formula uses the radian measure directly.

questions.title: Arc length, sector perimeter and rolling distance: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the arc length for radius 10 cm and angle 1.5 radians.
questions.hint_html: Use s = r theta.

questions.title: Arc length, sector perimeter and rolling distance: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A sector has arc length 17 cm and radius 7 cm. Find its perimeter in cm.
questions.hint_html: Include both straight radii.

questions.title: Arc length, sector perimeter and rolling distance: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A radius-8 cm circle has a minor arc angle 1.5 radians. Its major arc length is \((16\pi-k)\) cm. Find k.
questions.hint_html: Subtract the minor arc from the circumference.
questions.solution_html: The minor arc is \(8(1.5)=12\), so the major arc is \(16\pi-12\).

questions.title: Arc length, sector perimeter and rolling distance: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: An arc has length 7 cm. At the same radius, its angle is multiplied by 3. Find the new arc length in cm.
questions.hint_html: At fixed radius, arc length is proportional to angle.

questions.title: Sector area and a fixed-perimeter constraint: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the sector area for r=5 cm and angle 1.6 radians.
questions.hint_html: Use half the radius squared times the angle.

questions.title: Sector area and a fixed-perimeter constraint: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A radius-5 cm sector has area 10 square cm. Find its angle in radians.
questions.hint_html: Rearrange the sector-area formula.

questions.title: Sector area and a fixed-perimeter constraint: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A sector has area 28 square cm and arc length 7 cm. Find the radius in cm.
questions.hint_html: Combine A=r squared theta/2 with s=r theta.

questions.title: Sector area and a fixed-perimeter constraint: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: At a fixed angle, the radius is multiplied by 4. By what factor is the sector area multiplied?
questions.hint_html: Area scales as the square of the radius.

questions.title: Chords, minor segments and major segments: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: A sector has area 23 square cm and its central triangle has area 9 square cm. Find the minor segment area.
questions.hint_html: Subtract the triangle from the sector.
questions.solution_html: The segment area is \(23-9=14\) square cm.

questions.title: Chords, minor segments and major segments: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A radius-6 cm sector has angle \(\pi/2\). Its minor segment area is \((9\pi-k)\) square cm. Find k.
questions.hint_html: The triangle has perpendicular radii.
questions.solution_html: Triangle area is \(\tfrac12(6)(6)=18\); subtract it from \(9\pi\).

questions.title: Chords, minor segments and major segments: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A radius-11 cm circle has a chord subtending \(\pi/3\). Find the chord length.
questions.hint_html: The two radii and the chord form an equilateral triangle.
questions.solution_html: The chord length equals the radius, \(11\) cm.

questions.title: Chords, minor segments and major segments: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: In a radius-12 cm circle, the minor segment area is \(9\pi\) square cm. The major segment area is \(k\pi\) square cm. Find k.
questions.hint_html: Subtract from the disk area.

questions.title: Annular sectors and composite boundaries: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: An annular sector has radii 8 cm, 2 cm and angle 0.6 radians. Find its area.
questions.hint_html: Subtract the inner sector area.

questions.title: Annular sectors and composite boundaries: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: For annular-sector radii 8 cm, 2 cm and angle 0.6 radians, find the full perimeter.
questions.hint_html: Include both arcs and the two radial edges.

questions.title: Annular sectors and composite boundaries: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Two non-overlapping radius-5 cm sectors have angles 0.7 and 0.9 radians. Find the total area.
questions.hint_html: Add the two sector areas.

questions.title: Annular sectors and composite boundaries: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Two sectors each have area 18 square cm. Their overlap is 5 square cm. Find the union area.
questions.hint_html: Subtract the overlap once from the sum.

questions.title: Exact values, quadrants and general angles: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find \(\cos180^\circ\).
questions.hint_html: Use the unit circle on the negative x-axis.
questions.solution_html: The point is \((-1,0)\), so cosine is \(-1\).

questions.title: Exact values, quadrants and general angles: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find \(\tan135^\circ\).
questions.hint_html: Use reference angle 45 degrees and the quadrant sign.
questions.solution_html: Tangent is negative in quadrant II: \(\tan135^\circ=-1\).

questions.title: Exact values, quadrants and general angles: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: If \(\sin\theta=-5/13\) in quadrant III, find \(\cos\theta\).
questions.hint_html: Find cosine squared, then choose its quadrant sign.

questions.title: Exact values, quadrants and general angles: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Find \(2\sin(7\pi/6)\).
questions.hint_html: The reference angle is pi/6 and sine is negative.

questions.title: Trigonometric graphs, periods and transformations: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the amplitude of \(y=1-4\cos(3x)\).
questions.hint_html: Use the absolute outside multiplier.

questions.title: Trigonometric graphs, periods and transformations: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: The period of \(y=\sin(3x)\) is \(k\pi\) radians. Find k.
questions.hint_html: Divide the ordinary sine period by 3.

questions.title: Trigonometric graphs, periods and transformations: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the maximum of \(y=3+5\sin x\).
questions.hint_html: Sine has maximum 1.

questions.title: Trigonometric graphs, periods and transformations: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: How many vertical asymptotes does \(y=\tan x\) have on \(0<x<3\pi\)?
questions.hint_html: Tangent is undefined where cosine is zero.
questions.solution_html: The asymptotes are \(\pi/2,3\pi/2,5\pi/2\), three in total.

questions.title: Identities, factorisation and valid domains: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: If \(\sin x=3/5\) and \(\cos x=4/5\), find \(\tan x\).
questions.hint_html: Use the quotient identity.

questions.title: Identities, factorisation and valid domains: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Given \(\cos x=2/5\), find \(\sin^2x\).
questions.hint_html: Use sine squared plus cosine squared = 1.

questions.title: Identities, factorisation and valid domains: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Given \(\sin x=-3/5\), evaluate \((1-\cos^2x)/\sin x\).
questions.hint_html: Replace the numerator by sine squared.
questions.solution_html: The expression simplifies to \(\sin x=-3/5\); its denominator is nonzero.

questions.title: Identities, factorisation and valid domains: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: For any real x, evaluate \(2\sin^2x+2\cos^2x+3\).
questions.hint_html: Factor out 2 and apply the identity.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: How many roots does \(\sin x=-1/2\) have on \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.hint_html: Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV.
questions.solution_html: The roots are \(210^\circ,330^\circ\), so there are two.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the principal value of \(\sin^{-1}(-1/2)\) in degrees.
questions.hint_html: Use the principal range from -90 to 90 degrees.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: How many roots does \(\cos(3x)=0\) have on \(0\le x\le\pi\)?
questions.hint_html: Solve for 3x in the interval from zero to 3 pi.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: How many roots does \(\sin x=0\) have on \(-\pi\le x\le2\pi\)?
questions.hint_html: Include both endpoints.
questions.solution_html: The roots are \(-\pi,0,\pi,2\pi\), four in total.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: review variant 5
questions.prompt_html: Find the principal value of \(\cos^{-1}(1/2)\) in degrees.
questions.hint_html: Inverse cosine takes principal values between zero and 180 degrees.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: review variant 6
questions.prompt_html: Find the principal value of \(\tan^{-1}(1)\) in degrees.
questions.hint_html: Use the principal interval between -90 and 90 degrees.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: How many solutions does \(2\sin^2x+\sin x-1=0\) have on \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.hint_html: Factor as a quadratic in sine.
questions.solution_html: \((2\sin x-1)(\sin x+1)=0\); the roots are \(30^\circ,150^\circ,270^\circ\), three in total.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: How many solutions does \(2\cos^2x-\cos x-1=0\) have on \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.hint_html: Find the two allowed cosine values.
questions.solution_html: \((2\cos x+1)(\cos x-1)=0\). The roots are \(0,2\pi/3,4\pi/3\), three in total.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: How many roots does \(\sin x\cos x=0\) have on \(0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ\)?
questions.hint_html: Use both factors and retain the closed right endpoint.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: How many solutions does \(\tan^2x=0\) have on \(-\pi<x<\pi\)?
questions.hint_html: Only zero tangent values qualify; endpoints are excluded.
questions.solution_html: Only \(x=0\) lies in the open interval, so there is one root.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: review variant 5
questions.prompt_html: How many solutions does \(\sin x=\sqrt3\cos x\) have on \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.hint_html: Check the cosine-zero cases before using tangent.
questions.solution_html: The cosine-zero cases fail. Otherwise \(\tan x=\sqrt3\), giving \(60^\circ,240^\circ\): two roots.

questions.title: Arithmetic progressions: terms, sums and integer thresholds: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: An AP has first term 5 and difference 4. Find its seventh term.
questions.hint_html: Use a+(n-1)d.

questions.title: Arithmetic progressions: terms, sums and integer thresholds: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of \(2,6,10,\ldots\).
questions.hint_html: Use the first and tenth terms.

questions.title: Arithmetic progressions: terms, sums and integer thresholds: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: An AP has second term 7 and sixth term 19. Find its common difference.
questions.hint_html: The difference spans four term steps.

questions.title: Arithmetic progressions: terms, sums and integer thresholds: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: The numbers \(k,14,23\) are consecutive AP terms. Find k.
questions.hint_html: The middle term is the arithmetic mean.

questions.title: Geometric progressions: finite sums and convergence: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: A GP has first term 1 and ratio 3. Find its fifth term.
questions.hint_html: Use a times r to the power n-1.

questions.title: Geometric progressions: finite sums and convergence: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the sum of the first four terms of \(4,12,36,\ldots\).
questions.hint_html: Add four terms or use the finite GP formula.

questions.title: Geometric progressions: finite sums and convergence: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the sum to infinity of \(18,-9,4.5,\ldots\).
questions.hint_html: The ratio is -1/2.

questions.title: Geometric progressions: finite sums and convergence: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A nonzero GP has ratio \(-2/k\), with k positive. The convergence condition is \(k>a\). Find a.
questions.hint_html: The magnitude of the ratio must be less than 1.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in an arithmetic progression: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: The angles \(25^\circ,\theta,95^\circ\) are consecutive AP terms. Find theta in degrees.
questions.hint_html: Average the first and third angles.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in an arithmetic progression: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Angles form \(10^\circ,25^\circ,40^\circ,\ldots\). Find the seventh angle in degrees.
questions.hint_html: The common difference is 15 degrees.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in an arithmetic progression: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: The angles \(0^\circ,30^\circ,60^\circ\) are in AP. Find the difference between the sine of the second angle and the sine of the first.
questions.hint_html: Evaluate the sine values themselves.
questions.solution_html: \(\sin30^\circ-\sin0^\circ=1/2\). Nonlinear transforms need not preserve an AP.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in an arithmetic progression: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: \(\sin0^\circ,k,\sin90^\circ\) are consecutive AP terms. Find k.
questions.hint_html: Use the arithmetic mean of the two known values.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in a geometric progression: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: The angles \(5^\circ,20^\circ,\theta\) are consecutive GP terms. Find theta in degrees.
questions.hint_html: The common ratio is 4.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in a geometric progression: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: \(\cos60^\circ,k,\sin30^\circ\) are consecutive GP terms with k positive. Find \(k^2\).
questions.hint_html: The middle term squared equals the product of its neighbours.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in a geometric progression: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A GP has first term \(\sin90^\circ\) and ratio \(\cos60^\circ\). Find its infinite sum.
questions.hint_html: The first term is 1 and the ratio is 1/2.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in a geometric progression: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: For \(0<\theta<90^\circ\), a GP ratio is \(\tan\theta\). The convergence condition is \(\theta<a^\circ\). Find a.
questions.hint_html: The positive ratio must be below 1.

questions.title: Series models: accumulation, decay and repeated motion: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: A display has 10 tiles in its first row and 4 extra in every later row. Find the total for 10 rows.
questions.hint_html: Use an arithmetic sum.
questions.solution_html: The last row has 46 tiles, so the total is \(10(10+46)/2=280\).

questions.title: Series models: accumulation, decay and repeated motion: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A culture starts at 12 units and doubles hourly. How many units are present after 5 hours?
questions.hint_html: The initial amount is at time zero.

questions.title: Series models: accumulation, decay and repeated motion: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A machine releases 30 g in its first pulse and one third as much in every next pulse. Find the infinite total mass.
questions.hint_html: Use a convergent geometric sum.

questions.title: Series models: accumulation, decay and repeated motion: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A total starts at 80 and increases by a fixed 7 each month, without interest. Find the total after 6 months.
questions.hint_html: Use a fixed additive change, not compound growth.

questions.title: Finite binomial expansions and signs: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in \((1+3x)^4\).
questions.hint_html: Choose two factors supplying 3x.

questions.title: Finite binomial expansions and signs: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of x in \((2-x)^4\).
questions.hint_html: Choose one -x and three constant factors.

questions.title: Finite binomial expansions and signs: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the constant term in \((3+x)^4\).
questions.hint_html: Choose the constant from every factor.

questions.title: Finite binomial expansions and signs: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: How many nonzero terms occur in the expansion of \((1+x)^8\)?
questions.hint_html: Include the constant term.
questions.solution_html: The powers are \(x^0,x^1,\ldots,x^8\), giving nine terms.

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^3\) in \((1+x)^8\).
questions.hint_html: Use 8 choose 3.

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^4\) in \((3+x)^5\).
questions.hint_html: Four factors supply x and one supplies 3.

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the constant term in \((x+3/x)^4\), x nonzero.
questions.hint_html: If r factors supply 3/x, the total exponent is 4-2r.

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in \((2+5x)^3\).
questions.hint_html: Use the general term with r=2.

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: review variant 5
questions.hint_html: Cancel 6 factorial first.

questions.title: Coefficients in products and parity: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in \((1+2x)(1+3x)^2\).
questions.hint_html: Include both ways to make total power 2.

questions.title: Coefficients in products and parity: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of x in \((4-x)(1+2x)^2\).
questions.hint_html: Combine the constant-linear and linear-constant contributions.

questions.title: Coefficients in products and parity: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^3\) in \((1-2x)(1+x)^4\).
questions.hint_html: Subtract twice the x-squared coefficient from the x-cubed coefficient.

questions.title: Coefficients in products and parity: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in \((1+x+x^2)(1+2x+3x^2)\).
questions.hint_html: Use exponent pairs (0,2), (1,1), (2,0).

questions.title: Unknown constants and an unknown exponent: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: The x coefficient in \((1+kx)^6\) is 18. Find k.
questions.hint_html: The linear coefficient is 6k.

questions.title: Unknown constants and an unknown exponent: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: In \((1+kx)^5\), k positive, the coefficient of \(x^2\) is 40. Find k.
questions.hint_html: Use 10k squared.

questions.title: Unknown constants and an unknown exponent: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: In \((3+kx)^3\), the x coefficient is -81. Find k.
questions.hint_html: The coefficient is three times 3 squared times k.

questions.title: Unknown constants and an unknown exponent: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: The x-squared coefficient in \((1+kx)^4\) is 54. Enter the negative possible value of k.
questions.hint_html: Both signs solve the squared equation.

questions.title: Finite expansions as approximations: keep the remainder: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Use terms through \(x^2\) in \((1+x)^3\) to approximate \((1.02)^3\).
questions.hint_html: Substitute x=0.02 into 1+3x+3x squared.

questions.title: Finite expansions as approximations: keep the remainder: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Use \(1-4x+6x^2\) to approximate \((0.98)^4\).
questions.hint_html: Here x=0.02.

questions.title: Finite expansions as approximations: keep the remainder: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: At x=0.1, find the omitted part when \((1+x)^4\) is approximated by \(1+4x+6x^2\).
questions.hint_html: The omitted terms are 4x cubed plus x to the fourth.

questions.title: Finite expansions as approximations: keep the remainder: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: What is the greatest exponent of x in the finite expansion of \((2+x)^7\)?
questions.hint_html: There are seven linear factors.
questions.solution_html: The highest-power term comes from selecting x seven times: \(x^7\).

questions.title: Derivatives: powers, linear inner functions and domains: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=2x^3-5x\), find \(dy/dx\) at x=2.
questions.hint_html: Differentiate each term.

questions.title: Derivatives: powers, linear inner functions and domains: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=\sqrt{x}+x^{-1}\), find \(dy/dx\) at x=1.
questions.hint_html: Use rational powers before differentiating.

questions.title: Derivatives: powers, linear inner functions and domains: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=(2x+1)^3\), find \(dy/dx\) at x=1.
questions.hint_html: Include the derivative 2 of the inner function.

questions.title: Derivatives: powers, linear inner functions and domains: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: On \(y=x^2\), the chord from x=-2 to x=-2+h has gradient -4+h. Find the limiting gradient as h tends to zero.
questions.hint_html: Let the moving point approach x=-2.

questions.title: Tangents, normals and the zero-gradient case: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the tangent gradient to \(y=x^2+3\) at x=5.
questions.hint_html: Evaluate the first derivative.

questions.title: Tangents, normals and the zero-gradient case: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the normal gradient to \(y=x^2+1\) at x=2.
questions.hint_html: Use the negative reciprocal of the tangent gradient.
questions.solution_html: The tangent gradient is 4, so the normal gradient is \(-1/4\).

questions.title: Tangents, normals and the zero-gradient case: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: The tangent to \(y=x^2\) at x=3 is \(y=6x+c\). Find c.
questions.hint_html: The tangent passes through (3,9).

questions.title: Tangents, normals and the zero-gradient case: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: The normal at the vertex of \(y=(x-4)^2+2\) is \(x=k\). Find k.
questions.hint_html: A horizontal tangent has a vertical normal.
questions.solution_html: The vertex is \((4,2)\), and its normal is \(x=4\).

questions.title: Increasing, decreasing and stationary points: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x^3-12x\), find the second derivative at x=-2.
questions.hint_html: Differentiate twice.

questions.title: Increasing, decreasing and stationary points: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x^3-12x\), find the x-coordinate of its local minimum.
questions.hint_html: Solve for stationary points and check the second derivative.
questions.solution_html: \(y\prime=3x^2-12=0\) gives \(x=\pm2\); \(y\prime\prime(2)=12>0\), so the minimum has x=2.

questions.title: Increasing, decreasing and stationary points: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x^2-10x+7\), the decreasing interval is x less than a. Find a.
questions.hint_html: Set the first derivative equal to zero to locate the boundary.

questions.title: Increasing, decreasing and stationary points: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: For \(f(x)=x^4\), both first and second derivatives vanish at zero. Find the minimum value of f on [-1,1].
questions.hint_html: An inconclusive second-derivative test does not rule out an extremum.
questions.solution_html: \(x^4\ge0\), with equality at zero. The minimum is 0.

questions.title: Related rates and small increments: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x^2\), dx/dt=5. Find dy/dt when x=3.
questions.hint_html: Multiply dy/dx by dx/dt.

questions.title: Related rates and small increments: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A square side s grows at 0.75 cm/s. Find its area growth rate at s=8 cm.
questions.hint_html: Differentiate A=s squared with respect to time.

questions.title: Related rates and small increments: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A sphere radius grows at 0.5 cm/s. At r=3 cm, its volume growth rate is \(k\pi\) cubic cm/s. Find k.
questions.hint_html: Use dV/dt=4 pi r squared dr/dt.

questions.title: Related rates and small increments: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A length decreases steadily by 9 cm in 3 seconds. Find its signed rate in cm/s.
questions.hint_html: A decrease has negative signed rate.

questions.title: Optimisation on a feasible domain: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: A rectangle has perimeter 32 cm. Find the width giving maximum area.
questions.hint_html: For fixed perimeter, write A=w(16-w).

questions.title: Optimisation on a feasible domain: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the minimum of \(x+25/x\) for x positive.
questions.hint_html: Find the positive stationary point.

questions.title: Optimisation on a feasible domain: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the maximum of \(x^2\) on \([-2,4]\).
questions.hint_html: Check the stationary point and both endpoints.
questions.solution_html: The candidate values are 4, 0 and 16. The maximum is 16.

questions.title: Optimisation on a feasible domain: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A model gives area \(A(w)=w(10-w)\) for \(0\le w\le4\). Find the maximum area.
questions.hint_html: The unconstrained stationary width may be infeasible.
questions.solution_html: The stationary width is 5, outside the domain. A increases on [0,4], so its maximum is \(A(4)=24\).

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: An antiderivative of \(9x^2\) is \(ax^3+C\). Find a.
questions.hint_html: Divide by the new exponent 3.

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: An antiderivative of \((3x+2)^3\) is \(a(3x+2)^4+C\). Find a.
questions.hint_html: Account for the inner derivative and the exponent.

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Evaluate the improper integral \(\int_0^1x^{-2/3}\,dx\).
questions.hint_html: Use an antiderivative and a right-hand limit at zero.

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: For which exponent n is the ordinary power-integral formula for \((7x-1)^n\) invalid because n+1=0?
questions.hint_html: Identify the zero denominator.
questions.solution_html: The ordinary power formula excludes n=-1.

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: review variant 5
questions.focus: negative power with linear inner function
questions.prompt_html: For x greater than -2/5, an antiderivative of \((5x+2)^{-2}\) is \(a(5x+2)^{-1}+C\). Find a.
questions.hint_html: Differentiate the proposed antiderivative.

questions.title: Recover a curve from its gradient: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: A curve has dy/dx=6x-2 and passes through (1,-3). Write \(y=3x^2-2x+C\). Find C.
questions.hint_html: Use the point after integrating.

questions.title: Recover a curve from its gradient: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A curve has dy/dx=4x and y(1)=3. Find y(3).
questions.hint_html: Add the definite integral of the derivative to the initial value.

questions.title: Recover a curve from its gradient: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Given \(y\prime\prime=8x\) and \(y\prime(0)=-3\), find \(y\prime(2)\).
questions.hint_html: Integrate once and determine the constant.

questions.title: Recover a curve from its gradient: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A curve has derivative 2x and passes through (0,7). Find y(2).
questions.hint_html: The point determines the constant of integration.

questions.title: Signed integrals and geometric areas: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the area under y=2x above the x-axis from x=0 to x=3.
questions.hint_html: Integrate over the given interval.

questions.title: Signed integrals and geometric areas: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the total geometric area between y=x and the x-axis from x=-2 to x=2.
questions.hint_html: Split at zero and make both areas positive.
questions.solution_html: Two triangles each have area 2, giving total area 4.

questions.title: Signed integrals and geometric areas: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the area between \(y=3x\) and \(y=x^2\) from x=0 to x=3.
questions.hint_html: Integrate the upper curve minus the lower curve.

questions.title: Signed integrals and geometric areas: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: Find the area between y=9 and \(y=x^2\) for \(-3\le x\le3\).
questions.hint_html: The line is above the curve on this interval.

questions.title: Volumes of revolution: disks and washers: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: The region under \(y=\sqrt{x}\), 0 to 4, rotates about the x-axis. Find \(V/\pi\).
questions.hint_html: The disk area uses y squared, which equals x.

questions.title: Volumes of revolution: disks and washers: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: The region between \(x=y^2\) and the y-axis, 0 to 3 in y, rotates about the y-axis. Find \(V/\pi\).
questions.hint_html: Use radius x and integrate x squared with respect to y.

questions.title: Volumes of revolution: disks and washers: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: The region \(1\le y\le3\), \(0\le x\le2\), rotates about the x-axis. Find \(V/\pi\).
questions.hint_html: Subtract the inner disk area from the outer disk area.

questions.title: Volumes of revolution: disks and washers: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A washer has outer radius 5 cm and inner radius 2 cm. Its cross-section area is \(k\pi\). Find k.
questions.hint_html: Subtract squared radii, not the square of their difference.

questions.title: Accumulation and mixed calculus review: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: A flow rate is \(q(t)=3t+2\) litres/minute. Find the amount entering from t=0 to t=4.
questions.hint_html: Integrate the rate.

questions.title: Accumulation and mixed calculus review: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: An amount starts at 5 units and has rate \(dQ/dt=3t\). Find Q(4).
questions.hint_html: Add the accumulated change to the initial amount.

questions.title: Accumulation and mixed calculus review: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A quantity has signed rate \(2t-4\) from t=0 to t=3. Find its net change.
questions.hint_html: Integrate the signed rate, retaining negative contributions.

questions.title: Accumulation and mixed calculus review: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A quantity has rate \(3t-6\) from t=0 to t=4. Find its total variation.
questions.hint_html: Integrate the absolute rate and split at t=2.
questions.solution_html: The loss and gain each have magnitude 6, so the total variation is 12.

questions.title: Quadratics, functions and admissible solutions: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(f(x)=(x+2)^2+7\), x at least -2, enter the lower endpoint of the inverse domain.
questions.hint_html: The inverse domain is the original range.
questions.solution_html: The range is \([7,\infty)\), so the inverse domain starts at 7.

questions.title: Quadratics, functions and admissible solutions: review variant 2
questions.hint_html: Select the root satisfying the original restriction.
questions.solution_html: \(x+2=3\), so \(x=1\); the other algebraic root is excluded.

questions.title: Quadratics, functions and admissible solutions: review variant 3
questions.hint_html: Apply the inner translation before squaring.

questions.title: Quadratics, functions and admissible solutions: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: How many distinct real solutions does \((x+1)^2+5=14\) have?
questions.hint_html: Compare the right side with the minimum.

questions.title: Lines, circles and derivatives: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=2x^2+4x\), find the tangent gradient at x=1.
questions.hint_html: Differentiate the curve equation.

questions.title: Lines, circles and derivatives: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A tangent of gradient 8 passes through (1,6). It has equation y=8x+c. Find c.
questions.hint_html: Substitute the point.

questions.title: Lines, circles and derivatives: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the tangent gradient to \(x^2+y^2=25\) at (4,3), using radius geometry.
questions.hint_html: The radius and tangent are perpendicular.
questions.solution_html: The radius gradient is 3/4; the tangent gradient is -4/3.

questions.title: Lines, circles and derivatives: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: The normal to \(y=x^2\) at (2,4) meets the y-axis at (0,b). Find b.
questions.hint_html: Use normal gradient -1/4 and the given point.

questions.title: Trigonometric branches and sector models: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: A radius-8 cm sector has angle \(\pi/2\). Its arc length is \(k\pi\). Find k.
questions.hint_html: Use arc length = radius times angle.

questions.title: Trigonometric branches and sector models: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A radius-4 cm sector has angle \(\pi/2\). Its minor segment area is \((4\pi-k)\) square cm. Find k.
questions.hint_html: Subtract the right triangle from the sector.
questions.solution_html: The triangle area is \(4\cdot4/2=8\), hence the segment is \(4\pi-8\).

questions.title: Trigonometric branches and sector models: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: A radius-6 cm sector has angle \(60^\circ\). Its area is \(k\pi\) square cm. Find k.
questions.hint_html: Convert the degree angle to radians first.

questions.title: Trigonometric branches and sector models: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A radius-10 cm circle has a chord subtending \(\pi/3\). Find the chord length.
questions.hint_html: Use the isosceles triangle, or the chord half-angle formula.

questions.title: Coefficients as sequence data: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: An AP has \(u_n=4n+3\). Find the coefficient of x in \((1+x)^{u_2}\).
questions.hint_html: Evaluate the positive integer exponent first.
questions.solution_html: \(u_2=11\), and the linear coefficient in \((1+x)^{11}\) is 11.

questions.title: Coefficients as sequence data: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A GP is \(3,6,12,\ldots\). Let a be its third term. Find the x-squared coefficient in \((1+ax)^4\).
questions.hint_html: Find a, then use the binomial coefficient.

questions.title: Coefficients as sequence data: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the sum of the first three coefficients, in ascending powers, of \((1+x)^5\).
questions.hint_html: Include the constant coefficient.
questions.solution_html: The first coefficients are 1,5,10, with sum 16.

questions.title: Coefficients as sequence data: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: The first coefficients of \((1+x)^5\) are 1,5,10. Find the difference between the third and second coefficients.
questions.hint_html: Read the coefficients as a sequence before testing a progression.
questions.solution_html: The requested difference is \(10-5=5\); it differs from the first difference 4.

questions.title: Recovered curves, regions and accumulated quantities: review variant 1
questions.prompt_html: A model has \(Q(t)=t^3-4t^2+20\). Find its instantaneous rate at t=4.
questions.hint_html: Differentiate the output with respect to t.

questions.title: Recovered curves, regions and accumulated quantities: review variant 2
questions.prompt_html: A model has signed rate \(3t^2-6t\). Find its net change from t=0 to t=4.
questions.hint_html: Integrate the rate over the whole interval.

questions.title: Recovered curves, regions and accumulated quantities: review variant 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the minimum of \(Q(t)=t^3-6t^2+50\) on \(0\le t\le5\).
questions.hint_html: Compare stationary values and endpoint values.
questions.solution_html: The candidate t values are 0,4,5, with outputs 50,18,25. The minimum is 18.

questions.title: Recovered curves, regions and accumulated quantities: review variant 4
questions.prompt_html: A flow is constant at 4 litres/second for 7 seconds. Find the accumulated volume in litres.
questions.hint_html: Multiply the rate by the duration, with consistent units.
